back: A reaction in which the products can react to form the original reactants again; shown with ⇌.
Forward: left to right as written. Reverse (backward): right to left.

front: Energy changes of a reversible reaction
back: If the forward reaction is endothermic, the reverse is exothermic by the same amount.

front: How do you reverse the dehydration of copper(II) sulfate?
back: Heat blue crystals to make white anhydrous salt (endothermic); add water to turn it blue again (exothermic).

front: Cobalt(II) chloride: heating and adding water
back: Heating: pink → blue (water removed). Adding water or moist air: blue → pink.
NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g); the white solid re-forms in the cooler part of the tube.

front: Why does heating hydrated copper(II) sulfate in an open tube go to completion?
back: The steam escapes, so the reverse reaction cannot happen.

front: Is melting ice a reversible reaction?
back: No: it is a reversible physical change; no new substance forms.

front: Chromate(VI) / dichromate(VI): effect of acid and alkali
back: Acid turns yellow chromate(VI) orange (dichromate(VI)); alkali turns it yellow again.
